title: When the Summit Sings
premise: Bram Coldharbour and his storm-chasing crew owe a crushing debt to the Optimists, a cheerful syndicate that breaks legs with a smile. When Bram's old rival Vess Karrow dangles enough money to clear it, she buys their silence and their skills for one job: salvage the singing wreck of the Meridian Bell before the corporate fleet reaches it—six tides from now. The wreck sits in the Siren Shoals, waters the crew swore off after losing their fifth member there twelve years ago. As tides burn down, Bram discovers Vess intends to keep the wreck's resonance engine for herself, a power source that could enslave whole coastlines. In the end, Bram scuttles the engine into the deep rather than let anyone own its song, pays his debt with the truth instead of gold, and finally stops running—choosing his crew, his grief, and a home he never thought he deserved.
about_author: Theo Whitlock is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent nine years charting coastal wrecks before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who measure their lives in distances they're afraid to close.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A routine storm chase off Greywater Point goes wrong when the Optimists' collectors board mid-squall, smiling, reminding him of the debt: forty days. Introduces the crew—Juno the navigator, Pell the engineer, quiet young Wren. Emotional beat: Bram's practiced detachment cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Vess Karrow arrives at the dockside tavern with charts, coin, and an old grudge. She offers triple the debt to salvage the Meridian Bell from the Siren Shoals. Bram refuses; Juno quietly accepts on the crew's behalf. POV alternates Bram and Juno. Beat: betrayal of trust disguised as rescue.

chapters.title: What We Swore Off
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, flashback braided into present as the crew preps the kite-ship Halcyon. Twelve years ago they lost Tam in the Shoals; only Bram knows exactly how. Wren asks questions no one answers. Beat: guilt surfacing like something drowned coming up for air.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Departure under a dying wind. Vess rides along uninvited, her own fast launch trailing. Pell discovers the ship's ballast has been tampered with—someone wants them slow. POV Pell. Beat: paranoia takes root; the race clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: The Optimist's Smile
chapters.summary: A collector skiff intercepts them at sea—not to collect, but to warn: the Optimists have money on the Bell too. Bram realizes everyone hunting the wreck believes the debt will be paid one way or another. POV Bram. Beat: the trap tightening while the horizon stays beautiful.

chapters.title: First Tide: Dead Water
chapters.summary: The Halcyon enters the Shoals' outer ring where currents cancel and sails fail. Juno navigates by sound—the wreck's resonance hums through the hull. Wren hears it first and won't say what it sounds like. POV Wren. Beat: wonder shadowed by dread; the sea begins to sing.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Fleet's Wake
chapters.summary: They spot the corporate salvage fleet anchored at a supply atoll, three days ahead but stalled by a bribed harbor official—Vess's doing. Bram confronts her; she reveals she knows how Tam died, or claims to. POV Bram. Beat: old wounds weaponized; trust erodes further.

chapters.title: Third Tide: The Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: First dive. The Meridian Bell hangs intact in a cathedral of coral, its resonance engine still faintly alive after twelve years. Pell confirms it could power a city—or a weapon. POV Pell. Beat: awe curdling into fear of what they've found.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: What Sang to Tam
chapters.summary: Wren dives alone against orders and surfaces changed, humming a melody no one taught her. Juno realizes the engine broadcasts to the living, not just machines. POV Juno. Beat: the past repeating; maternal terror beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Vess's True Chart
chapters.summary: Bram finds Vess's real manifest: she's not salvaging for a buyer—she means to seize the engine herself and sell dominion over every resonant coast. Confrontation; she doesn't deny it. 'Invisible men don't get to be moral.' POV Bram. Beat: the rival becomes the true antagonist.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: A storm builds as the crew fractures: some want Vess's payday, some want the engine destroyed, Wren wants to answer the song. Juno locks the dive gear away. POV Wren. Beat: belonging tested—family arguing like family, which is worse.

chapters.title: The Debt Comes Due
chapters.summary: Optimist collectors board at anchor, smiling wider than ever. They offer to forgive everything if Bram delivers the engine intact. He signs nothing; they leave a bomb as collateral. POV Bram. Beat: survival priced in someone else's future.

chapters.title: Storm Chaser's Instinct
chapters.summary: With the bomb armed and the fleet inbound, Bram does what he does best: reads weather. There's a channel through the Shoals only rideable inside the storm itself. He proposes the impossible run. POV Bram. Beat: competence as redemption; the runner deciding to steer toward danger.

chapters.title: Riding the Singing Gale
chapters.summary: The storm run. Full-crew sequence—Juno calling bearings, Pell trimming, Wren listening to the Bell's song through the gale to find the channel. They thread it; the fleet loses two ships trying. POV rotates. Beat: the crew remembering why they belong together.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide, Turned
chapters.summary: At the wreck, Vess holds Wren at hook-point, demanding the engine core. Bram offers himself and the truth of Tam's death as trade: Tam died saving Bram from the engine's first test, and Bram has run from that ever since. POV Bram. Beat: confession as currency; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Song Takes Hold
chapters.summary: Vess raises the core anyway; its full song erupts, bending water and minds alike. Collectors, fleet survivors, everyone in the Shoals falls under its pull except those who've already surrendered something—Bram, grieving openly for the first time. POV Wren. Beat: power revealed as hunger; corruption audible.

chapters.title: Scuttle the Bell
chapters.summary: Climax. Pell rigs the engine's housing to flood; Bram dives through the song to set the charge while Vess fights Juno above. The Bell sinks into the trench, its song fading to a single note, then silence. Vess escapes empty-handed into the storm. POV Bram underwater. Beat: sacrifice without martyrdom—he chooses loss over ownership.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: The Shoals go quiet for the first time in twelve years. The collectors' bomb is found disarmed—Pell had gutted it days ago, gambling on Bram's choice. The debt stands, unpaid in coin. POV Pell. Beat: exhausted relief; luck acknowledged honestly.

chapters.title: Paying With Truth
chapters.summary: Bram sails to the Optimists alone and gives them something better than the engine: the location records of three wrecks they didn't know existed, plus testimony that ends their salvage monopoly's insurance. The debt dissolves—not forgiven, but traded. POV Bram. Beat: the runner learning to negotiate instead of flee.

chapters.title: What Wren Heard
chapters.summary: Wren reveals the song wasn't a lure—it was a memory, the engine recording twelve years of the Shoals. Inside it was Tam's last message, meant for the crew all along. They listen together. POV Wren. Beat: grief given voice; the dead allowed to speak.

chapters.title: Anchorage
chapters.summary: The Halcyon moors at Greywater Point, not passing through. Juno takes the harbormaster's post, Pell opens a workshop, Wren enrolls in the navigator's school. Vess sends a single line from across the sea: 'Next time, Coldharbour.' POV Juno. Beat: roots put down deliberately, not by default.

chapters.title: When the Summit Sings
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Bram's POV. He climbs the headland above town at dawn—the summit he always measured in miles and never reached—and finds he can hear the sea from here, faintly, holding no song at all. He stays until sunset. Beat: resolution; a man who counted miles learns, at last, to count years.
